title: Angara orders stronger mental health programs in schools
summary: Education Secretary Sonny Angara has issued an order aimed at boosting mental health programs in schools amid the increase in the incidents of suicide among learners.

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Education Secretary Sonny Angara has issued an order aimed at boosting mental health programs in schools amid the increase in the incidents of suicide among learners.

Angara signed DepEd Order No. 024, s. 2026 on Nov. 26 directing all concerned school officials in both public and private elementary and secondary schools and local universities and colleges to implement the School-Based Mental Health Program (SMHP), which aims to promote learners’ mental health and well-being, prevent further mental health risks and provide responsive intervention to learners.

“The guidelines aim to set the national framework for mental health promotion and care in basic education; lay out the processes and procedures relevant to the various components of the program, as shown in the framework, including those related to systems strengthening and enumerate the roles and responsibilities of DepEd offices across governance levels and schools in the implementation of the SMHP,” Angara said in his order.

In the Philippines, the 2019 Global School-Based Student Survey estimated that among learners aged 13 to 17, 23.1 percent – including 18.8 percent among males and 27.1 percent among females – have seriously considered attempting suicide, while 24.3 percent, or 19.9 percent among males and 28.4 percent among females, have already attempted suicide.
The Department of Education (DepEd) said data also show that the COVID-19 pandemic may have exacerbated mental health challenges and risks for children and adolescents.

DepEd said that the Philippine General Hospital reported an increase in adolescent consultation from 17 percent pre-pandemic to 27 percent during the pandemic, with anxiety and depression as the most related mental health problems.
